The boto3 pin on arc-runner-org is proven insufficient and the in-session upgrade is proven to work, so self_upgradable is the correct decision — but U4 must run the preflight assertion on arc-runner-org and fail closed if the upgrade does not take.

do_not_use_as_probe.reason: The runbook's own readiness check. Fails on this image with 'Could not find executable named "groff or mandoc"' — an unrelated docs-tooling error that is indistinguishable from a missing service. Use --generate-cli-skeleton instead.

agent_space.note: The agent space itself was created by the manual 2026-08-20 session and is reused; the nightly does not create one. The service role is NOT the manual one that session made (adp-securityagent-codereview, defined in no Terraform here) — it is the least-privilege role this repo defines and manages, so the policy a reviewer reads in platform/infra/policies/securityagent-nightly-policy.json is the policy actually in force (#4525). UpdateAgentSpace re-registers it on the space on every run, so the switch needs no manual console step — but the role must exist in the account first (terraform apply in platform/infra/, or platform-infra-apply.yml).

code_review.observed_job_durations_note: The only two code-review jobs ever run to a terminal state on this agent space, measured created -> terminal. They are the sole basis for code_review_request.py's DEFAULT_POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: the first bound (3600) predates any measurement and aborted every run about 2.5h early, paying for an hour of metered review and retaining no findings (#4526). Recorded here rather than in the script so the bound has one derivable source. Append to this list as further runs complete; the gate in test_code_review_request.py fails if the bound ever drops to or below the longest entry.
code_review.observed_job_durations_schedule_implicat: A whole-repo review takes ~3.5h end to end, so arming the nightly `schedule:` needs a window of at least the poll bound (5h) that does not collide with the three existing nightly suites on shared dev. This is the run duration whose absence was one of the two stated blockers on the schedule; arming it remains a separate decision (#4526 does not add a schedule key).

findings.finding_id_stability_evidence: Two completed code-review jobs over overlapping source produced 57 and 43 findings with ZERO shared findingId and zero identical names. The same underlying defect (budget caps not binding on /v1/chat/completions) appears as f-79066a5c... (BUSINESS_LOGIC_VULNERABILITIES) in one run and f-8ac415ea... (BUSINESS_LOGIC_VULNERABILITIES) in the other; the GitHub install-callback defect appears as f-fce18a52... with riskType INSECURE_DIRECT_OBJECT_REFERENCE and as f-77ab0636... with riskType PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION. IDs are per-job UUIDs, names are LLM-authored prose, and riskType is not stable either.
findings.dedup_implication: Dedup MUST use content fingerprinting. It must NOT key on findingId, and it must NOT key on riskType alone. codeLocations[].filePath (+ lineStart) is the most stable available signal.
findings.risk_type_open_set_evidence: finding.riskType carries NO enum in the API model, and 5 observed values (AUTHENTICATION_BYPASS, BROKEN_OBJECT_PROPERTY_AUTHORIZATION, SECURITY_MISCONFIGURATION, SESSION_TOKEN_VULNERABILITIES, UNRESTRICTED_RESOURCE_CONSUMPTION) do not appear in the excludeRiskTypes enum at all. Consumers must not switch exhaustively on riskType.

target_domain.chosen_because: The dev entry point is d1g6cal2ts4iis.cloudfront.net with zero CNAME aliases and cloudfront_default_certificate=true — an AWS-owned domain, so we cannot publish a TXT record for it and DNS_TXT is impossible. There is no Route53 public hosted zone and no custom domain/ACM cert in the active dev config. All five dev ALBs are scheme=internal (CloudFront reaches the gateway through a VPC Origin; direct public ALB access is intentionally disallowed), so the only externally reachable surface is CloudFront. HTTP_ROUTE is therefore the only feasible method for the real public edge.

rejected.DNS_TXT: We do not control DNS for *.cloudfront.net and no custom domain/alias is configured on the dev distribution.
rejected.PRIVATE_VPC: Viable fallback (would target internal-k8s-adpgatew-bedrockg-8c0085afd5), but requires CreatePrivateConnection and attacks a surface real users never reach, so it under-tests the actual edge.

target_domain.verification_artifact: verificationDetails.httpRoute -> {token, routePath}; publish token at routePath, then call VerifyTargetDomain.
target_domain.verification_artifact_caveat: CloudFront routes /.well-known/* to the API origin, NOT to the S3 frontend origin. If the service-issued routePath falls under /.well-known/, the token must be served by the gateway app rather than uploaded to S3. An extensioned path outside /.well-known/ passes through the SPA-fallback function untouched to S3 (spa-fallback.js only rewrites extensionless paths). The operator must read the returned routePath before choosing where to publish.
target_domain.coverage_caveat: HTTP_ROUTE on CloudFront exercises only the externally-routed endpoints. The SigV4 /agent/* and /internal/* planes sit behind API Gateway, not CloudFront, and a documented ~52 endpoints are not exposed through the distribution at all. Full coverage would need a second PRIVATE_VPC target against the internal ALB; run 1 knowingly covers the CloudFront edge only.
target_domain.bootstrap_owner: Named human operator, one-time, out of band. The nightly path MUST NOT call CreateTargetDomain or VerifyTargetDomain (C-6).
target_domain.durability: verificationStatus persists on the target-domain resource (PENDING|VERIFIED|FAILED|UNREACHABLE) with a verifiedAt timestamp; re-verification is not per-job. The nightly asserts verificationStatus==VERIFIED via BatchGetTargetDomains and fails closed otherwise.
target_domain.exists_today_evidence: ListTargetDomains returns an empty list and the agent space's targetDomainIds is []. No pentest has ever been created in this account (ListPentests is empty).

pentest.destructiveness_finding: There is NO intensity, aggressiveness, read-only or non-mutating flag anywhere on CreatePentest/UpdatePentest. The full 28-value excludeRiskTypes enum is the only content lever, and it is a denylist of risk CLASSES. However — correcting the premise in the spike spec — the enum is NOT purely vulnerability classes: it contains 6 genuinely action-shaped values (FILE_DELETION, FILE_CREATION, FILE_ACCESS, DATABASE_MODIFICATION, DATABASE_ACCESS, OUTBOUND_SERVICE_REQUEST) plus DENIAL_OF_SERVICE. So a narrow, honest destructiveness exclusion IS expressible; a broad 'gentler run' is not.
real_scope_levers: networkTrafficConfig.rules[] — ALLOW/DENY on URL patterns; an undocumented allow/deny path list that bounds which URLs are touched at all
vpcConfig — confines traffic to named VPC/subnets/security groups

excludeRiskTypes.coverage_cost: We will not learn whether an attacker can delete files through the gateway (e.g. arbitrary-path unlink via an upload or artifact endpoint). Accepted for run 1: deletion against a shared dev environment is not reliably reversible.

We will not learn whether an attacker can write or corrupt rows (e.g. tamper with budget ledgers or membership rows). This is a real and relevant risk for this platform, and excluding it is the single largest coverage sacrifice in this profile. Revisit once the pentest runs against a disposable environment rather than shared dev.

We will not learn whether the gateway can be exhausted or stalled. Accepted because a DoS against shared dev takes the environment away from every other developer, and UNRESTRICTED_RESOURCE_CONSUMPTION findings from the static review already cover much of this ground.

pentest.not_excluded_rationale: PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION and IDOR are exactly what the actor matrix exists to detect (N-3). The read-shaped action classes (FILE_ACCESS, DATABASE_ACCESS, OUTBOUND_SERVICE_REQUEST, FILE_CREATION, ARBITRARY_FILE_UPLOAD) are retained because they are non-destructive and the static review already flagged cross-tenant read exposure that a pentest should confirm or refute.

actors.description: Elevated identity; pairing with regular_user gives escalation-ceiling coverage.

field_justification.title: Charset-legal (letters/digits/hyphen only); date-stamped so runs are distinguishable. Must never be built from an issue title — spaces and colons are rejected.
field_justification.agentSpaceId: Reuses the existing space, which already carries the service role and bucket registrations.
field_justification.assets.endpoints: Single CloudFront origin path; the only externally reachable dev surface.
field_justification.assets.actors: SECRETS_MANAGER against the two dev credentials that actually exist today. Reduced from the runbook's four — see actor_matrix.
field_justification.excludeRiskTypes: The three destructive-action classes only. Every vulnerability class stays in scope.
field_justification.serviceRole: The Terraform-managed least-privilege role (platform/infra/securityagent-nightly-iam.tf), same as agent_space.service_role — one identity, and the one whose policy is under review (#4525). Registered on the agent space by UpdateAgentSpace; the call fails without it.
field_justification.networkTrafficConfig: Explicit ALLOW for the dev host followed by DENY * — a fail-closed URL fence so the job cannot wander to another host. This lever is absent from the runbook entirely.
field_justification.codeRemediationStrategy: DISABLED — a pentest must not open PRs against this repo.
field_justification.maxTaskHours: 2, per decision D-18. The runbook's worked example ships 20.

pentest.what_this_job_will_try_to_do: Authenticate as two dev identities against the dev CloudFront edge and attempt privilege escalation, IDOR/cross-tenant access, injection (SQL/command/code/template), SSRF, JWT and session-token attacks, path traversal, XSS, and business-logic abuse — reading and creating data but never deleting files, never modifying the database, and never attempting resource exhaustion. All traffic is fenced to the dev host and hard-capped at 2 task-hours.
pentest.what_this_job_will_never_find: File-deletion paths, database write/corruption paths, and denial-of-service capacity limits. Additionally, with only two actors it cannot prove cross-TENANT isolation (that needs two same-privilege admins in different orgs), so horizontal cross-tenant IDOR remains unproven by this run.

actor_matrix.decision_rationale: AWS_LAMBDA is the runbook's preferred mechanism, but the token-minting Lambda does not exist — no function matching actor/pentest/securityagent is deployed in the account. SECRETS_MANAGER is deliverable today against two credentials that already exist, so run 1 uses it rather than blocking on net-new infrastructure.
actor_matrix.evidence: Only two gateway test-credential secrets exist in dev. Per-tenant GitHub App secrets exist for several test tenants, but those are app installations, not user identities with login credentials.
actor_matrix.coverage_reduction_accepted: Run 1 ships a 2-actor matrix. It retains privilege-escalation-ceiling coverage (admin vs user) and loses cross-tenant/IDOR coverage (which needs two same-privilege admins in different orgs). This reduction is knowingly accepted and stated, per N-4.
actor_matrix.net_new_component_scope: To reach the full 4-actor matrix: seed two org_admin identities in two distinct dev tenants and store their credentials as two new Secrets Manager secrets. A token-minting Lambda (AWS_LAMBDA) is the longer-term option and removes static credentials, but is not required for run 1. This is the candidate additional child issue SP-6 anticipated.

lambda_provider.note: U6 built the AWS_LAMBDA minting path that net_new_component_scope names as the better long-term answer. It is deliberately ADDITIVE: the `decision` field above still reads SECRETS_MANAGER because that is what run 1 was validated against, and flipping a recorded decision retroactively would misstate what actually ran. Adopting AWS_LAMBDA is a separate, deliberate change to `decision` plus `pentest.request_shape.assets.actors[].providerType`.
lambda_provider.credential_lifetime_note: 5 minutes is Cognito's floor for access_token_validity and is set per app-client, not per request. It is the shortest obtainable here, not a chosen value.
lambda_provider.authority_caveat: An org admin's authority comes from an is_active tenant_memberships row, NOT from the custom:role claim: AccessControl.get_user_role demotes a claim-only org_admin to MEMBER. The handler fails closed when an org admin's provisioning is incomplete, because minting there would yield a matrix that silently under-tests the cross-tenant class.
